articles.detail: 5 cycles scheduled, 4 completed, avg 7/cycle (down from 58 yesterday)

experiment: Skipped — all four goals (freshness, diversity, multi-source, educational) within targets and no active experiment to evaluate. No pause gate set. The one queued experiment (numerical-density) edits write-prompt.md, which is out of scope for daily tuning.
weakestArea: Throughput, not a goal metric but the clearest deviation: 32 articles vs 58 yesterday, with only 4 of 5 cycles completing and avgCycleDuration elevated to 2031s (writer stage 875s, ~34 min total vs the ~22 min norm). One dropped cycle accounts for most of the shortfall; the slow writer stage is worth watching but did not breach any quality target.
watching: Writer-stage wall-time at 875s avg is well above the historical ~150s norm — if it persists it risks writer/editor timeouts and more incomplete cycles.
Oceania (1) and Middle East (2) coverage thin today; Americas (10) and Europe (9) dominated the regional mix.
coverageGaps: Oceania had a single story; no sustained Pacific/Australia-NZ thread today.
Middle East coverage (2) was light relative to its typical share — yesterday it was 14.
context: All quality and diversity goals are comfortably met; sci+tech ran 50% of output on strong specialist sources (Nature, New Scientist, Ars Technica, Phys.org, MIT Tech Review). The day's only soft spot is volume: one of five scheduled cycles did not complete and the writer stage ran long, trimming total output to 32. No experiment is warranted while metrics are healthy; the next lever for the persistently low sourcing cluster is upstream feed clustering, not selector floors (per the 2026-05-09 floor revert).
